market_question: Will the Republicans win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
reasoning: The 2028 election is an open race with no incumbent, and historical baseline for such elections is close to 50%. The market prices Republicans at 38.5%, which seems too pessimistic given typical structural advantages (e.g., Electoral College tilt) and the lack of a clear Democratic frontrunner three years out.
evidence_points: Open-seat presidential elections since 1900 have averaged near 50% for the out-of-power party, with no strong bias below 40%.
Republicans will hold the White House until 2028, which typically gives a modest advantage due to incumbency of the administration (though not the candidate).
Current polling for 2028 is sparse, and early betting markets often overweigh recency bias; no credible analyst assigns a sub-40% chance this far out.
